endonym.gloss: the jar that is kept alive

description.value: A narrow fired jar with a shoulder seal of brine crust, buried to the neck in the floor of an interdune hollow and opened at intervals of nine or ten days. Jars carry a household's working culture and are the measure of a household: people are described by the number of jars they brought through the last bad year, and the number is given before the name. This one was traded out in 2288 after it had been scoured and its culture lost, which the household regarded as the end of the object and the collection did not. The neck is chipped on one side from the lifting tool and the brine crust survives in patches.
